points.text: Claim of much better results than other pixel-space models contradicted by RDM and PixelFlow.
'Nearly 8x faster' claim does not match Table 1.
DPG score in text (0.82) differs from table (80.9).
Placeholder 'abc steps' and missing hyperparameters harm reproducibility.
Presentation errors: undefined dimensions, inconsistent names, duplicated paragraph, misplaced symbols, typos.
Several citations point to wrong papers.
Motivating VAE-induced errors and artifacts are not measured.
The paper's own samples contain blurry regions.
Gain over latent models unclear without latent models trained with the same recipe.
Compute parity and comparable quality versus latent models not tested with matched-recipe control.
Central ablation relies on training loss and qualitative pair; no baseline FID reported.
No control separating predicted per-patch weights from a static shared MLP head.
Benefit of feeding noisy pixels into decoder (skip path) not separated from neural field.
Lower-memory claim contradicted by ADM-G memory in Table 1.
8x speedup figure matches no ratio in Table 1.
Per-step times inconsistent with per-image times for baselines in Table 1.
Training speed slower than pixel baseline.
Efficiency measurement conditions unstated and baselines run in different frameworks.
Headline result uses unmatched sampling budget; no NFE column.
CFG scale and interval tuned on the evaluation metric.
Single runs, no seeds or variance; solver differences within noise.
Text-to-image comparisons confounded by text encoder, data and SFT; no matched control.
Reproducibility gaps: placeholder fine-tune steps, undefined symbols, missing optimizer, batch, GPU-hours, code.
Parameter count of weight-predicting layer not reported.
Minor issues: duplicated paragraph, naming typos, undefined symbols, Eq. 1 notation.
Copied baseline numbers in Tables 2/3 not marked as such.
DPG score in text (0.82) inconsistent with Table 5.
CFG interval differs between Table 3 caption and Section 4.4.
Output normalization description inconsistent between equations and ablation text.
Training-free arbitrary resolution shown only qualitatively.
Handling of seams and block artifacts between patches not examined.
DCT-basis encoding lacks normalization and its suitability is not justified.
Arbitrary-resolution generation resembles learned upsampling; not quantitatively evaluated.
Latency and memory measured under unstated hardware, batch and precision.
Scaling to higher resolution and larger patch sizes not examined.
No broader-impact, misuse or data licensing discussion for text-to-image model.
Qualitative samples are curated; random grids needed.
No baseline FID to isolate mechanism.
No static-head control to isolate mechanism.
No skip-input control to isolate mechanism.
Lower-memory claim contradicted for ADM-G.
8x speedup matches none of the computed ratios.
Training slower than pixel baseline.
T2I gains confounded by text encoder, recaptioning, SFT data and prompt rewriting.
Superiority wording over pixel-space models contradicted by RDM and PixelFlow.
Comparison to latent counterparts across different recipes without matched run.
Arbitrary resolution only qualitative; transformer sees resampled input.
REPA/DINOv2 external prior undermines no-pretrained-component narrative; no REPA-off result.
'abc steps' placeholder.
CFG interval inconsistency between Table 3 and Section 4.4.
Citations point at wrong papers.
Qualitative samples are selected.
Novelty moderate; no empirical comparison with nearest alternatives like INRFlow or conv decoders.
Pixel-space positioning misworded; RDM and PixelFlow outperform on FID/sFID.
Recent pixel-space comparators at 512 missing.
Citation errors, including the VAE-artifact motivation reference.
VAE accumulated-error and artifact motivation not quantified.
PixNerd itself produces blurry details.
Model introduces its own blurry or unnatural artifacts.
Neural field head adds complexity; performance sensitive to its depth, channels, normalization.
Training instability requiring specific normalization to avoid loss spikes.
Unclear what is specifically designed beyond the original NeRF MLP head.
Results at 512 resolution less convincing; degradation unexplained.
No comparisons at higher resolutions such as 768 or 1024.
8x latency claim unclear about comparison models and unsupported by Table 1.
Training memory nearly doubled compared with latent counterpart.
Performance at 512 scales worse than at 256, falling behind SiT-XL.
Rectified flow citation missing.
Table 4 should state it reports ImageNet256.
Necessity unclear given distilled few-step diffusion; can PixNerd serve as distillation teacher?
Claimed speedup still slower than VAE plus diffusion pipelines.
Missing baselines in Table 1: StyleGAN-XL, CDM, Simple Diffusion, VDM++, PaGoDA.
No quantitative and latency comparison with one-step GAN or distilled models.

DPG score mismatch between text and table.
Placeholder fine-tune steps and missing hyperparameters/code hurt reproducibility.
Presentation errors, typos, duplicated paragraph, undefined symbols.
Wrong citations.
VAE-artifact motivation not measured.
PixNerd samples show blurry details.
No matched-recipe latent baseline for quality and compute comparison.
Ablation uses losses only; no baseline FID.
No static-weight head control.
No noisy-pixel skip-input control.
Memory claim contradicted for ADM-G.
Per-step vs per-image time inconsistency in Table 1.
Training slower than pixel baseline.
Efficiency measurement conditions unstated.
Unmatched sampling budget; no NFE column.
CFG tuned on evaluation metric.
No variance or seeds reported.
T2I comparison confounded by encoder, data, SFT.
Weight-predicting layer parameter count not reported.
Copied baseline numbers not marked.
CFG interval inconsistency.
Normalization description inconsistent.
Arbitrary-resolution claim only qualitative.
Patch seams and block artifacts unexamined.
DCT encoding choice and normalization unjustified.
Scaling to higher resolution and patch sizes unexamined.
No ethics or data licensing statement.
Curated qualitative samples.
Dependence on REPA/DINOv2 prior; no REPA-off result.
Moderate novelty; no comparison with closest alternatives.
Missing recent pixel-space 512 comparators.

Q.summary: Novelty beyond NeRF MLP head unclear.
Still slower than VAE plus diffusion pipelines.
No comparison with one-step models incl. latency.
